analysis.investment_thesis: Brigade scores poorly on both Magic Formula legs — an earnings yield of ~6.1% (EBIT INR 1,421 Cr / EV ~INR 23,295 Cr) barely clears the 6% floor, while ROCE of 13.3% sits well below my 20% threshold. Real estate developers consume enormous capital and produce lumpy, debt-laden returns that the Magic Formula was not designed to reward.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 10.7% over 9 years with clear acceleration in FY24-25 (INR 4,897→5,074 Cr)
OCF positive all 5 years; FY25 operating CF of INR 995 Cr shows improving cash conversion
Equity nearly doubled to INR 6,481 Cr in FY25 (likely QIP), strengthening the balance sheet
key_risks: Gross debt of INR 5,950 Cr (D/E 0.76) constrains financial flexibility in a rate-sensitive sector
ROCE of 13.3% and ROE of 14.9% are both below cost-of-capital thresholds for high-quality compounders
Finance costs of INR 495 Cr (FY25) consume ~35% of EBITDA, limiting true free cash flow
red_flags: Net profit was negative in FY21 and FY22, revealing the cyclicality and fragility of earnings
Capex surged to INR 639 Cr in FY25 versus INR 269 Cr in FY24, inflating capital base and suppressing ROIC
Real estate is explicitly a sector the Magic Formula ranks poorly — capital intensity destroys the EBIT/capital ratio
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Brigade's EV of roughly INR 23,295 Cr (mkt cap INR 18,644 Cr + debt INR 5,950 Cr – cash INR 1,299 Cr) against EBIT of INR 1,421 Cr yields an earnings yield of only ~6.1% — barely above the reject threshold. More critically, ROCE of 13.3% signals that every rupee invested in this business earns mediocre returns; the Magic Formula demands 20%+ to enter the 'good business' column. The EV/EBITDA of 15.3x further confirms the valuation is stretched for the quality on offer.

The operational trajectory is improving — net profit grew from negative territory in FY21-22 to INR 680 Cr in FY25, and the leasing/hospitality mix adds recurring revenue. But the structural problem remains: real estate requires continuous capital recycling, finance costs are permanently elevated, and the business will never score well on ROIC. I need businesses that earn high returns on incremental capital; Brigade consumes capital to generate below-par returns.
